page_note: Page contains a natural-process correspondential teaching about pearl formation: rain drops descend, enter oysters, mingle, are molded into pearls of varying number depending on how the drop divides. This is classic substrate correspondential science — describing a natural process that maps to a cosmic process (drops of light into matter producing precious souls/forms). The teaching is heavily damaged but coherent. Editorial fatigue score is high because the second half contains a pedagogical recap pivot at seg 25 ('Behold, I have taught you...' / 'I have said to you that...'), which is hortatory application voice wrapped around the same teaching reiterated. After the recap, the teaching resumes with pearl-divers (32-34). Substrate dominates; the pedagogical voice intrudes only at the recap seam.
